content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (p95 latency also climbing). Initial spike at 1963002468. Auto-escalation sent to #eng-oncall.

kevin.sre: I'm up — looking at metrics now. noticing sustained CPU on g4s and many small requests triggering overhead.

maria.prod: customer impact: a handful of medium customers reporting increased latency and truncated responses. Support ticket count +7 in last 10m.

lee.runtime: adding context — continuous batching queue depth is pretty high, but the engine is doing tiny per-request batches because many clients use low token limits. That causes high per-token overhead.

ana.support: @maria.prod linking the most affected customer IDs in case we need to throttle: CUST-1023, CUST-7781. Tickets 4521 and 4523.

kevin.sre: first-order mitigation options: 1) global safe-rate-limit (short term) 2) bump batching window to increase aggregation (trade latency) 3) per-tenant quota throttle for noisy tenants 4) disable streaming/early-flush which increases churn. Thoughts?

maria.prod: prioritize preserving availability for interactive customers. If we must trade latency for throughput that's acceptable for some customers. Prefer per-tenant throttle first for the top noisy ones.

lee.runtime: I can push a live runtime config that increases the batching aggregation window from 20ms -> 120ms and enables conservative prefix caching for identical prompts. That should reduce request headcount and amortize kernel overhead. We'll see latency p50=>+30ms but p95 should drop overall when the queue empties.

kevin.sre: ok push plan: (A) apply per-tenant soft quota to CUST-1023 and CUST-7781 (limit to 60rps each) (B) increase batching window to 120ms across the affected pool (C) temporarily disable streaming for new connections from noisy tenants (D) deploy traffic-shaper rule to reduce concurrency per connection from 8->4. I'll coordinate with opsbot for rate-limit rules.

opsbot: running playbook: rate-limit patch v2 queued. ETA 30s to apply to us-west-2 egress.

lee.runtime: preparing runtime patch. Config snippet I'm about to apply: ```json
{
  "pools": ["us-west-2-inference-a"],
  "batching": {
    "max_latency_ms": "120",
    "min_aggregation_ms": "40",
    "max_batch_tokens": "8192",
    "continuous_batching": "enabled",
    "kv_cache_prefetch": "conservative"
  },
  "streaming": {
    "enabled": "false",
    "disable_for_tags": ["noisy-tenant"]
  }
}
```

maria.prod: is that a hot reload or requires a rolling restart? we need zero customer restarts.

lee.runtime: hot reload supported for batching params. Streaming toggle will apply to new sessions only; existing sessions unaffected.

kevin.sre: opsbot, apply per-tenant quota now. use dry-run for 60s then hard limit if signals good.

opsbot: per-tenant rate limit applied (dry-run): CUST-1023@60rps, CUST-7781@60rps. Dry-run window 60s.

ana.support: customers notified in tickets about temporary rate-limiting as mitigation. message: "we're throttling high-volume requests to preserve availability; expect reduced latency within minutes."

kevin.sre: watch graphs for dropped queues, CPU reduction, and 5xx rate. I'll monitor infra trace for tail latencies.

lee.runtime: live metrics: queue consolidation increasing, avg batch size +3x in the last 40s. kernel occupancy improved.

kevin.sre: 5xx rate trending down from 3.2% -> 0.9% over last 2 minutes. good sign.

maria.prod: ticket update sent. Support to escalate if customer still impacted after 5m.

lee.runtime: rolling apply of batching config complete for pool us-west-2-inference-a. No restarts.

opsbot: rate-limit dry-run positive: 95th percentile error reduction for noisy tenants. Converting to enforced limit in 10s.

kevin.sre: enforcing per-tenant quota now.

ana.support: customers CUST-1023 & CUST-7781 report stabilization, some higher P50 latency but no errors.

lee.runtime: we also disabled dynamic streaming for new sessions tagged noisy-tenant. That reduced token churn significantly.

kevin.sre: next step: decide whether to keep batching window at 120ms or step it down to 80ms. proposal: keep 120ms for 15m stabilization, measure p50/p95. If p95 improves without hurting p50 too much, consider a gradual rollback.

maria.prod: agree. Put rollback plan in case third-party customers complain. Also prepare customer communication template for sustained changes.

opsbot: scheduling 15m check-in: 1963003368. Reminder will post summary metrics.

lee.runtime: one-off tweak we applied: adjusted continuous batching parameter 'max_idle_ms' to 2000 to keep partially filled KV caches active longer — this reduces rewarm cost at expense of memory.

kevin.sre: note for postmortem: root cause hypothesized as surge of many low-token requests increasing scheduling overhead and hitting kernel inefficiencies. Mitigations: batching-window tuning, per-tenant throttles, streaming disable, traffic shaping.

maria.prod: handoff note: I'll be taking the next shift; @lee.runtime please ping me on any rollback.

lee.runtime: will do. leaving a short runbook snippet for follow-up: ```
- If p95 rises > 2000ms after 15m: revert batching.max_latency_ms to 80 and re-enable streaming for non-noisy tenants.
- If 5xx > 1%: rollback streaming disable immediately and scale up pool by +2 nodes.
- If CPU stays > 85%: reduce per-connection concurrency to 2.
```

kevin.sre: final state at 1963003068: 5xx at 0.6%, avg batch size +2.9x, p50 +32ms, p95 -150ms. Marking incident as mitigated but monitoring for full resolution.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager resolved. :white_check_mark:
